U-W100-00.title: Data Readiness Sprint: verify MaterialRegistry + published data coverage
U-W100-00.description: BLOCKING prerequisite. (1) Verify MaterialRegistry has thermal_diffusivity, cp, Lm, melting_point for D2, 304SS, 6061, WC, Inconel 718 — if missing, populate from ASM Handbook Vol. 1. (2) Extract additional cutting conditions from downloaded PDFs (Mitsubishi FA catalog, Sodick manual, Reliable EDM Ch5) to supplement the 10 existing data points. Target: ≥20 published data points (lowered from 40 per data librarian review). (3) Verify Klocke Ra k_ra values: published range is 0.35-0.42 for steel, NOT 0.13-0.23 as in current engines. (4) Verify DiBitonto K1=4.8 transfers from sinker to wire EDM — if not, fit K1 from ITW SHAKEPROOF real offset data. (5) Widen exit gate tolerances to ±15% (from ±5%) per published literature scatter.

U-W100-31.title: Wire break recovery: M20 re-thread + N-block restart markers
U-W100-31.description: CRITICAL production requirement (#1 failure mode per machinist review). Add to G-code output: (1) N-block numbers at every profile transition and pass change for safe restart. (2) M20 auto-re-thread sequence after each profile (between start holes). (3) Wire break recovery logic: detect break position, re-thread, approach from correct side, resume at last N-block. (4) Setup sheet: restart procedure for operator. Controller-specific M-codes: Mitsubishi M20/M21, Sodick M50/M51, Makino M60/M61, AgieCharmilles M50/M51.

U-W100-31.exit_criteria: N-blocks at every transition. M20/M50/M60 per controller. Restart procedure in setup sheet. 5 dialects tested.

U-W100-32.title: Slug management: physics-driven tab placement + drop sequence
U-W100-32.description: Slug drop on internal features is a constant shop floor concern. Wire EDMWireSlugCornerTaperEngine already has slug weight calculation and EDMToolpathStrategyEngine has tab logic — this unit WIRES them into the pipeline and validates. (1) Auto-calculate slug weight: W = A × t × ρ. (2) Tab placement: physics-driven from slug weight vs tab shear strength. (3) Drop sequence: cut tabs LAST, warn if slug exceeds machine table limit. (4) Safety: flag slugs >0.5kg as requiring support fixtures.

four_loop.build: Wire slug/tab engines into WEDMCompleteOrchestrationEngine toolpath stage
four_loop.scrutinize: /prism-review — verify weight calculation, tab strength, drop sequence safety
four_loop.gap_fill: Test: internal pocket with known area → correct slug weight → tabs placed → drop sequence correct
four_loop.tie_up: Setup sheet includes slug handling notes. Heavy slugs flagged.

abort_criteria: Tab shear strength data not available for validation materials
Slug weight calculation disagrees with manual calculation by >10%
Tab placement algorithm fails for complex geometry (>8 internal features)
U-W100-32.exit_criteria: Slug weight calculated. Tabs auto-placed. Drop sequence in G-code. Heavy slugs flagged. Wired to orchestrator.

U-W100-33.title: Flushing strategy engine: submerged vs jet auto-selection
U-W100-33.description: Wrong flushing on thick sections = wire break every 2 min. EDMCuttingParamFlushEngine has flushing logic but it's not wired to auto-select mode. (1) Auto-select: submerged for thick (>80mm) or enclosed geometry, jet for thin (<10mm) or open profiles. (2) Pressure scaling: thick sections need higher pressure for debris evacuation. (3) Nozzle gap: tighter for finish passes. (4) Validate flush pressure is within machine pump capability.

four_loop.build: Wire flushing auto-selection into orchestrator. Add pressure scaling from thickness.
four_loop.scrutinize: /prism-review — verify pressure scaling physics, machine pump limits
four_loop.gap_fill: Test: 10mm thin section → jet mode. 100mm thick → submerged + high pressure.
four_loop.tie_up: Flush mode in setup sheet. Pressure per pass documented.

abort_criteria: Flush pressure model produces unreasonable values (>15 bar)
Auto-selection disagrees with published guidelines for >30% of test cases
Machine pump data not available for validation
U-W100-33.exit_criteria: Auto-select flush mode from geometry + thickness. Pressure scales with thickness. Machine limits checked.

U-W100-34.title: Sodick + Makino controller dialect expansion
U-W100-34.description: Sodick uses C### condition codes (not E-pack), SF-Liner technology databases, and M50/M51 threading. Makino uses HYPER-i conditions, HyperCut multi-pass, and G51 taper mode. Currently these produce wrong technology codes. (1) Sodick: C### code generator from material group + thickness. (2) Makino: HYPER-i condition mapper. (3) Both: correct M-codes, program header format, coordinate precision. (4) Validate against Sodick and Makino programming manual references.

four_loop.gap_fill: Test: generate program for each controller, verify technology codes are valid format
four_loop.tie_up: Both dialects produce structurally correct, machine-parseable output

abort_criteria: Cannot find Sodick C### code format documentation

Generated codes fail basic format validation
U-W100-34.exit_criteria: Sodick C### codes generated correctly. Makino HYPER-i conditions mapped. Programs parseable by respective controllers.

U-W100-35.title: AgieCharmilles + Fanuc dialect expansion
U-W100-35.description: AgieCharmilles uses ISPG/IPG technology codes and TAPER-EXPERT for taper (NOT UV on G1). Fanuc Alpha uses technology registers and G61.1/G64 corner control. (1) AgieCharmilles: ISPG code mapper, TAPER-EXPERT cycle for taper mode. (2) Fanuc: technology register mapper, corner control codes. (3) Both: correct M-codes, header format, G-code structure. (4) Note: UV-on-G1 is NOT universal — AgieCharmilles uses proprietary taper cycle.

four_loop.scrutinize: /prism-review — verify taper handling differs per controller

four_loop.tie_up: All 5 dialects produce correct, machine-specific output

Fanuc technology register format varies by machine generation
Cannot validate without reference programs for these controllers
U-W100-35.exit_criteria: AgieCharmilles ISPG codes + TAPER-EXPERT. Fanuc tech registers + corner control. All 5 dialects complete.
